interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The postoperative pathology revealed a Gleason 4+4 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT2. The surgical findings noted, "There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was present; there was no lymph node metastasis." The presence of lymphovascular invasion is an adverse finding. Countervailing to this, the report documented "there was no lymph node metastasis." Seminal vesicle invasion was not documented as present.

The prognosis is influenced by the positive surgical margins and the presence of lymphovascular invasion. The absence of lymph node metastasis is a reassuring finding. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, which means biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing postoperative PSA or its trajectory would be crucial information to revise the prognosis. The current findings suggest a risk profile influenced by the positive margins and LVI, balanced by the negative nodal status. The fixed estimated horizon is 43.11 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 34.49–51.73 months; its coverage has not been validated.
